newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-YOUNG STEERS NEW ZEALAND INTO LEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YOUNG STEERS NEW ZEALAND INTO LEAD.

text.p: A grafting innings of 29 not out from opener Bryan Young enabled New Zealand to reach 49 for one wicket in their second innings at tea on the second day of the first test against Pakistan on Friday.

Earlier Simon Doull had collected his best test figures of five for 46 as Pakistan recovered superbly from their drastic overnight position of 52 for five to reach 191 all out and a first innings lead of 36.

The Pakistani recovery was masterminded by wicketkeeper Moin Khan who scored a resolute 59 and shared important parterships of 48 for the sixth wicket with Salim Malik and 56 for the seventh with Saqlain Mushtaq.
Salim had made 21 before he became Doull's fifth victim, edging high to second slip where Young took a good overhead catch.

Moin brought up his fourth half-century with his ninth four, driving off-spinner Dipak Patel through midwicket. He was eventually trapped lbw by seamer Justin Vaughan who collected each of the last four wickets to wrap up the innings shortly after lunch and collect his best test figures of four for 26.
New Zealand got off to a solid start in their second innings as Young and Vaughan put on 46 for the first wicket before Vaughan was bowled around his legs by Mushtaq Ahmad for 11.
Adam Parore replaced him and was two not out at the interval with New Zealand leading by 13.
